Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 03 s. 2023 January 11, 2023 MR. ANDREW DE GUZMAN 30andrew18@gmail.com Dear Mr. De Guzman: This has reference to your electronic mail dated October 13, 2022 which was forwarded to this Department by the Office of the Ombudsman, requesting guidance on the following issues, quoted herein in toto: 2. Is DILG obligated to respond to emails or (hardcopy) letters even if the receiving DILG Field Office or DILG Provincial Office were only in the "cc" letter or email distribution list? However, considering that the circumstances involved in the above- mentioned narration such as unanswered letter requests despite numerous follow ups between September 2020 and February 2021, or five months of unresolved, unanswered transactions with Government Units/Offices, these enabling circumstances shouldn't already be an alarming situation vis-å-vis 15-day RA3019 and 3-7-20 day RA 11032, for the DILG Field Office to act motu proprio, taking into consideration that DILG Field Office and DILG Provincial Office were only "cc" and not the actual addressees in the letter or email requests? The herein request stemmed from your allegations that your requests addressed to the LGU, copy furnished the DILG Field Office, for more than two years already have not been acted upon. Per your representation, in September 2020, February 2021 and December 2021, your family sent out letter requests to, and duly stamped received by, the following: • Office of the Mayor • Office of the Vice Mayor and Sangguniang Bayan • Sangguniang Barangay • Sangguniang Kabataan • DILG was included as "cc" in said letter requests From time to time, you sent out to same Offices numerous follow ups via messenger through their respective official facebook accounts but still, the same is not acted upon, except that the concerned DILG Field Office acknowledge receipt of March 2022 email, and specifically mentioned that they did not receive the emails in December 2021 and February 2021. Be it noted that the DILG Field Office was not copy furnished in the request dated September 2020. Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan"

As of today, your request has not been answered, hence, the herein instant queries. For the this Department, generally as a standard procedure, when furnished with a copy of a written request or document addressed to another government agency, public officer or private entity, performs the following: a. Acknowledge receipt of the request or document; b. Inquire in writing from the addressee the action taken thereon, copy furnished the letter-sender; or c. Refer the request or document to the appropriate office/offices, copy furnished the letter-sender. However, there are instances that this Department takes an appropriate action on the request/document, depending on the tenor or nature of the request/document, coupled with an assessment as to whether or not the request/document is within the Department's mandate. On the second quem considering the period that has already lapsed since you sent out your letters that were never responded by the addressees, you are hereby advised to already consider Section 1, Rule XIII of the Implementing Rules and Regulations of Repüblic Act No. 11032 or the Ease of Doing Business and Efficient Government Service Delivery Act of 2018, thus: "RULE XIII VIOLATIONS, JURISDICTION, PENALTIES, AND IMMUNITY Section I. Violations under the Act The following shall constitute violations of the Act and these Rules and Regulations: a) b) c) d) e) O g) h) Refusal to accept application or request with complete requirements being submitted by an applicant or requesting party without due cause; Imposition of additional requirements other than those listed in the Citizen's Charter; Imposition of additional costs not reflected in the Citizen's Charter; Failure to give applicant or requesting party a written notice on the disapproval of an application or request; Failure to render government services within the prescribed processing time on any application and/or request without due cause; Failure to attend to applicants or requesting parties who are within the premises of the office or agency concerned prior to the end of official working hours and during lunch break; Failure or refusal to issue official receipts; and Fixing and/or collusion with fixers in consideration of economic and/or other gain or advantage." (Emphasis supplied) Page 2 of 3

For rendition Of government service, the prescribed processing time pursuant to Section 1, Rule IV of the IRR of RA No. 11032 are as follows: (1) three (3) days for simple transactionsl; (2) seven (7) days for complex transactions2; and (3) twenty (20) working days for highly technical transactions3 or for applications or requests involving activities which pose danger to public health, public safety, public morals, public policy. Administrative and criminal liability arises for failure to render government services within the prescribed processing time on any application and/or request without due cause. We respectfully note that your letter did not specify the concerned LGUs nor their officials so that this Department, in the exercise of its delegated power of general supervision over local governments, could either: a. Inquire in writing from the addressee the action/s taken thereon, copy furnished the letter-sender; or b. Refer the request or document to the appropriate office/offices, copy furnished the letter-sender. Accordingly, if you believe that the concerned officials indeed failed to render government services as discussed above, you may file the appropriate complaint with the Anti-Red Tape Authority in accordance with Rule XIV of the IRR of RA No. 11032. This opinion is being rendered based on our appreciation of the queries and facts you presented and this is without prejudice to any contrary opinion of other competent authorities and/or the courts. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY RITY OF THE SECRETARY: AN VICTOR R. LLAMAS U e ecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs JVRULLLS-LRALLD/rrao/c1p Copy furnish: ATTY. JAMES Q. VIERNES Acting Director, Public Assistance Bureau Office Of the Ombudsman Ombudsman Building, Agham Road Diliman, Quezon City 1 Simple transactions — applications or requests submitted by applicants or requesting parties of a government office or agency which only require ministerial actions on the part of the public officer or employee, or that which present only inconsequential issues for the resolution by an officer or employee of said government office. 2 Complex transactions — applications or requests submitted by applicants or requesting parties of a government offce which necessitate evaluation in the resolution of complicated issues by an offcer or employee of said government ofice, such transactions to be determined by the office concerned. Highly technical application or transaction — a transaction which requires the use of technical knowledge, spedalized skills and/or training in the processing and/or evaluation thereof. Page 3 of 3
